title: Unified Inverse-Walk Upper Mixing Bound
summary: The odd-characteristic proof uses three-term arithmetic progressions unavailable in characteristic two; a unified inverse-walk mixing upper-bound proof remains open.

formal_statement.body: Develop a unified proof of the inverse-walk upper mixing bound over finite fields that applies in both odd characteristic and characteristic $2$. The existing odd-characteristic strategy produces $3$-cycles by first constructing a three-term arithmetic progression, but that intermediate construction has no counterpart in characteristic $2$; the unresolved task is therefore to obtain one upper-bound argument that works in both regimes.

scope.domain: Mixing bounds for inverse-generated random walks on permutations over finite fields.
parameters: Field characteristic — distinguishes the odd-characteristic and characteristic-2 regimes that a unified proof must cover
scope.unresolved_remainder: Find a single proof of the inverse-walk upper mixing bound that applies in both characteristic regimes.

citations.label: How Fast Does the Inverse Walk Approximate a Random Permutation?

progress.summary: The paper presents characteristic-dependent upper-bound strategies and asks whether a common approach exists. It identifies the absence of a characteristic-two analogue of the three-term arithmetic-progression step as an obstacle.
citation_labels: Vishesh Jain et al., How Fast Does the Inverse Walk Approximate a Random Permutation?
